To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ability to learn a visuomanual coordination task depends on the age of the subjects and on the conditions of learning, and that these conditions affect both the accuracy of the movements and the ability to integrate proprioceptive information.

the role of ongoing visual information in the acquisition of a new visuomanual coordination varies with age, and that children's learning is more sensitive than adults' to the spatial error of the movement.
the learning of a visuomanual coordination is influenced by the age of the learner, by visual feedback, and by the nature of the errors that the learner makes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of visuomanual coordination, with a particular emphasis on the role of vision during learning.
the development of visuomotor control and the role of ongoing visual information in children and adults.
the role of ongoing visual and proprioceptive feedback and of spatial error in learning a visuomanual task in young children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

children's learning of a visuomanual coordination task is more sensitive than that of adults to the absence of ongoing visual feedback, and is also more sensitive to spatial errors, particularly in the direction of the movement.

, at least in the visuomanual coordination studied, children's learning is slower and more difficult than adults' learning, and that this difficulty is due to both a lack of integration of proprioception and a lack of ability to use spatial information about errors to correct the movements.
the role of visual feedback in learning a visuomanual coordination task depends upon age, and that this role changes with age.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
children have difficulties in integrating proprioceptive feedback and that ongoing visual feedback is required to learn the task.
the role of ongoing visual information and of spatial errors is similar for children and adults in the acquisition of a visuomotor coordination.

, during the acquisition of a visuomanual coordination, children are more dependent than adults on visual information, and are also less efficient in integrating proprioception in order to control the spatial accuracy of their movements.
